Dosage Form(s): Acceptable dosage forms for all NHPs
Cream; Emulsion; Foam; Gel; Liquid; Lotion; Ointment; Paste; Pressed powder; Salve; Solution; Suspension; Topical liquid
Acceptable dosage forms for NHPs not containing nano titanium dioxide or nano zinc oxide
Aerosol; Aerosol, spray; Loose powder; Spray; Spray (bag-on-valve)
Acceptable dosage forms for NPDs
Aerosol; Aerosol, spray; Cream; Emulsion; Foam; Gel; Lotion; Ointment; Paste; Powder; Salve; Solution; Spray; Spray (bag-on-valve); Stick; Suspension

Use(s) or Purpose(s): Secondary sunscreens have a function other than sun protection while still providing the skin and lips protection from UV rays, i.e. moisturizers, make-up, lip balm, anti-ageing, anti-wrinkle creams.
All products (mandatory)
Sun Protection Factor "X"/SPF "X" *
Products with a critical wavelength of ≥ 370 nm ** and with medicinal ingredient(s) that provide UVA and UVB protection (optional)
Broad spectrum
Absorbs throughout the UVA/UVB spectrum
UVA/UVB protection
Products that are water resistant *** (optional)
Water/Sweat Resistant [40 minutes/80 minutes]
Note: For NPDs, products making any of the above claims are eligible for the labelling flexibilities set out in section 2.6 of the Labelling requirements for non-prescription drugs guidance document except for the warning statement regarding the risk of rashes, as mentioned in the Risk information section below.
* As determined using a standardized and reproducible method, such as the one referenced in US FDA 2021 M020 monograph, ISO 24444, ISO 23675 or ISO 23698. The SPF value must be ≥ 2 and values greater than 50 are to be declared as SPF 50+.
** As determined using a standardized and reproducible method, such as the one referenced in US FDA 2021 M020 monograph, ISO 24443, ISO 23698 or Colipa 2011

Use(s) or Purpose(s): *** As determined using a standardized and reproducible method, such as the one referenced in US FDA 2021 M020 monograph or Colipa 2005. When the Colipa methodology is used, the labelled SPF value must be the SPF value of the final product formulation determined following immersion (Antoniou et al. 2008).
Unacceptable use(s) or purpose(s)
See Appendix 1 .
Notes
PA rating (Protection grade of UVA)
The PA rating system was developed in Japan and is currently used by most Asian countries.
This system addresses UVA protection based on the Persistent Pigment Darkening method (e.g., ISO 24442).
For NPD ingredients, data must be provided to NNHPD through the labelling only submission pathway to support any additional information regarding the PA rating.
For NHP products containing zinc oxide or a combination of zinc oxide and titanium dioxide, the PA rating is acceptable as additional information on the label, as long as it is truthful and not misleading. Valid data using a standardized and reproducible method must be available upon request. This does not apply to titanium dioxide alone which is less effective at blocking long-wave UVA (UVA I) rays.
Subpopulation(s): Infants 6 to 12 months, Children 1 to 11 years, Adolescents 12 to 17 years, Adults 18 years and older

Direction(s) for use: Products excluding sprays and aerosols
Apply as needed
Spray and aerosol products
Apply as needed
Hold container 4 to 6 inches/10 to 15 centimetres from the skin to apply
Do not spray directly onto face. Spray on hands then apply to face
Do not apply in windy conditions
Use in a well-ventilated area
Avoid inhaling or exposing others to spray
All products (optional)
Test on a small area of skin before first use. If irritation occurs (within 24 hours), use a different product.

Caution(s) and warning(s): All products
For external use only
When using this product avoid contact with eyes. If contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water (US FDA 2021).
Stop use and ask a health care practitioner/health care provider/health care professional/doctor/physician if rash occurs ****
Keep out of reach of children. If swallowed, call a poison control centre or get medical help right away.
**** Note: For NPDs, this warning statement must appear on the outer label of all secondary sunscreen products, and is ineligible for Level 4 Graduated and Labelling for Low-Risk Non-prescription Drugs (Category I) flexibilities as described in the Guidance Document: Labelling Requirements for Non-prescription Drugs .

Contraindication(s): All products
Do not use on broken skin (US FDA 2021)
